name: information_ratio_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: The information ratio (IR = alpha / tracking_error relative to NIFTY 50) computed on rolling intraday data identifies which stocks are currently generating the best risk-adjusted alpha. By computing the 60-bar rolling IR for all NIFTY 50 stocks and entering the top 3 by IR (in their current direction), we systematically allocate capital to stocks with the strongest risk-adjusted outperformance. Stocks with high positive IR are generating consistent alpha above the index; stocks with low/negative IR are lagging. The inefficiency exists because IR is a portfolio evaluation metric (monthly/quarterly), not typically used as a real-time stock selection tool at 1-min frequency.
mechanism: Institutional order flow arrives in bursts via algorithmic execution (TWAP/VWAP slicing), creating persistent directional pressure over 30-120 seconds. Retail and smaller participants follow the initial move, extending momentum before liquidity absorbs the flow and the order book rebalances.

conditions: Info_Ratio > 1.0 (minimum IR threshold for quality signal)
Alpha_60 > 0 (positive alpha, not just low tracking error)

exit.signal_exit: IR_Rank drops out of top 10 (for longs) or rises above bottom 10 (for shorts)

filters.volume_filter: Selected stocks must have volume > SMA(volume, 20)

weaknesses: Information ratio on 60 1-min returns is statistically unreliable — with 60 observations, the estimated IR has a standard error of approximately 1/sqrt(60) ≈ 0.13, making the threshold of 1.0 barely distinguishable from 0.87
Top-3 ranking creates a competitive selection problem — on quiet days, even the top-ranked stock may have IR barely above zero, and we're selecting the 'least bad' rather than 'genuinely good'

The strategy is essentially momentum-on-alpha — stocks that have outperformed recently tend to continue. But at 60-bar lookback on 1-min data, this captures only 1-hour persistence which may not extrapolate
prior_art: Information ratio concept from Grinold & Kahn (2000) 'Active Portfolio Management'; momentum factor (Jegadeesh-Titman); cross-sectional momentum used in Fama-French models; intraday application is novel
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
